archetype.name: Bubble Team (goalie-dependent)
archetype.definition: A roughly break-even five-on-five team whose place in or out of the playoff picture will be decided by which goalie plays and whether the finishing holds up, not by its shot share.

report.headline: Even play, leaky crease: the Blues' season turns on Hofer, not the skaters
report.take:
Eight games in, St. Louis looks a lot like the team it was last year with a slightly better engine. The skaters are holding their own: a 50.2% xGF % and 52% CF % put them in the middle of the league or a touch above, an improvement on last season's 49.3% expected share. The 3-4-1 record and 23rd place on the site come from what happens at the ends of the ice. The offense ranks 9th in goals a game while sitting 21st in Shots / GP. The defense ranks 24th in goals against even though it allows a league-average number of shots.

Goaltending is the clearest problem, and it is a split problem. Joel Hofer has been fine: a .906 save %, +1.3 GSAx and a shutout in five starts. Jordan Binnington has been the opposite, at .831 and -5 GSAx in three starts. That one goalie accounts for more than the team's whole -3.1 Goalies GSAx, which ranks 24th. The opening week fits that split. A 4-0 win in Dallas came right before a 1-6 loss in Colorado, and the 2-5 loss in Nashville was much the same story. Last year's team also finished deep in the red on goaltending (-7.2 GSAx), so this is not a new weakness, but it is a fixable one if Hofer takes the net.

The numbers point in two directions. The 5-on-5 PDO of 95.9 is well below average, which says even-strength bounces have gone against them. The all-situations figures tell a different story: skater shooting is 13%, 8th in the league and well above the league's 11.3%. That high conversion has kept the scoring respectable on a low shot volume, and it is the piece most likely to fade. The Pts vs Goal Diff of -1.6 (28th) also says the record is a bit worse than the goal margin. Overall this is close to a .500 team that has been unlucky in tight games and bad in one crease.

One structural issue looks real. Opposing centers are piling up points against this defense: 4.5 a game, last in the league, and a 46.8% share of the points allowed against a league norm near 38%. Colton Parayko's 42.6% xGF % in over 21 minutes a night fits that, while the lighter-minute pair of Adam Jiricek and Justin Barron has driven play. Up front, Mason McTavish is the engine, 12th on the centers tab with 9 points and 29 shots, while Robert Thomas sits 110th. Where this goes depends on Hofer's workload, on the middle of the ice tightening up, and on whether the offense can find more shots before its shooting luck runs out.

strengths.title: Middle-of-the-pack possession, slightly improved
strengths.body: The Blues are winning a small share of the shot attempts and breaking even on expected goals at 5-on-5, a step up from last season's sub-50% share. Most of the forward group's regulars sit above 54% xGF %, so the improvement is spread across the lineup rather than carried by one line. That kind of process tends to hold, and it gives the record room to catch up.

strengths.title: McTavish driving the attack
strengths.body: Mason McTavish leads the forwards in points and shots in only 16 minutes a night and ranks 12th on his tab. His 57.4% xGF % says the production is backed by real chance creation, not just bounces. He is the best case for the offense holding up as team shooting cools.

strengths.title: A penalty kill that has flipped
strengths.body: The kill is at 84%, 9th in the league and well above the league average. Last year it ran under 77%. Eight games is a small sample for special teams, but this is a meaningful early turnaround for a unit that cost them last season.

concerns.title: Binnington's starts are sinking the crease
concerns.body: The team save % of .877 ranks 24th, and almost all of the damage comes from Binnington's .831 and -5 GSAx. Hofer's numbers are above average. The team's goaltending can recover quickly, but only if the starts tilt toward the goalie who is actually stopping pucks.

concerns.title: Scoring rests on high shooting
concerns.body: The Blues rank 9th in goals a game while ranking 21st in shots on goal, because skaters are converting 13% against a league average of 11.3%. Without more volume, the goal output should drift down toward the middle of the league as that rate normalizes.

concerns.title: Centers are feasting on this defense
concerns.body: Opposing centers are scoring well above their own averages, the worst mark in the league, and they take an outsized share of the points against. That points to trouble defending the middle. The top pairing's poor expected-goals share in heavy minutes suggests it is not just bad luck.

trend.note: The results have swung between blowout wins and lopsided losses rather than following a line. The last five games ran hotter at both ends, at 4 goals scored and 3.6 allowed a game, for a .500 points %.

weekAhead.headline: Four at home, two against the league's best
weekAhead.body:
After an opening run played mostly on the road, St. Louis gets four straight home games, though the middle of the week is brutal. Carolina is first on the site and the real thing: a 58.6% xGF %, 60% CF % and 33.1 shots a game. That will test a defense already giving up too much through the middle. Vegas is third with the league's best goal differential, but it is riding a 104.1 5-on-5 PDO and kills penalties at only 73.9%. That is the opening for a Blues power play that has been ordinary.

The bookends are more winnable. Winnipeg's 4-2-2 is padded by close-game luck (Pts vs Goal Diff +1.4) over a 46.7% xGF %, but its 30% power play ranks 3rd, so the Blues' improved kill matters. Montréal plays well but has a .868 save %, 28th in the league, and its defense lets wingers and defensemen outscore their norms. A split of the four games would be a solid result; how many points they take from the Jets and Canadiens shapes the week.

keyMatchups.title: Blues' kill vs Jets' power play
keyMatchups.body: Winnipeg's power play is 3rd in the league at 30%, while the Blues have killed 84% of penalties. Against a Jets team that does not out-chance anyone at 5-on-5, special teams are their main route to goals. Holding them there makes this a game the Blues should win on process.

keyMatchups.title: Surviving Carolina's shot volume
keyMatchups.body: The Hurricanes control play as well as anyone, putting 33.1 shots a game on net and allowing only 22.9. That is exactly the game where a sub-.880 team save % gets exposed. This is Hofer's night, if it is anyone's.

keyMatchups.title: Testing Montréal's soft goaltending
keyMatchups.body: The Canadiens' .868 save % and 28th-ranked defense are a good matchup for a Blues team that has been finishing at a high rate. Montréal also lets wingers outscore their averages. That should suit Snuggerud, who has 4 goals on 20 shots.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts in goal against Vegas and Carolina: if Hofer gets both, the Blues can steal points; if Binnington's numbers don't turn, the losses will be lopsided.

restOfSeason.body:
The 72-point pace undersells this team. The 5-on-5 play is even, the close-game luck has run against them, and team goaltending is being dragged down by one goalie's three bad starts. Regression toward average save percentage helps them more than any other change could. Working the other way, skater shooting at 13% on modest shot volume should cool, so goals for will likely settle closer to the league's 3.1 a game than to the current 3.38.

Net, this looks like last year's 86-point team with slightly better process and a better kill. That is a bubble team in a Central Division where the pack is tightly bunched early. The weakness down the middle and the blueline's lack of scoring (two goals from the listed defensemen) cap the ceiling. A real playoff push needs Hofer carrying most of the starts at his current level and the top pairing turning around its expected-goals share.
swingFactors: Shooting % cooling on low shot volume

confidence.note: Eight games; goalie splits rest on three to five starts each.
